Dana K. Whitfield
Department of Chemistry, Lakeshore University, Evanston, IL 60208 | dana.whitfield@example.edu

RESEARCH INTERESTS
Exciton migration and charge transport in organic semiconductor crystals; vibronic coupling and coherence in
molecular aggregates; ion transport in nanoconfined polymer membranes; open quantum systems theory for
energy transfer.

EXPERTISE
Ultrafast spectroscopy: broadband transient absorption (TA), two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES),
two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy (2DIR), time-resolved infrared (TRIR)
Theory and simulation: hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM), Redfield theory, density functional theory (DFT)
Electrochemistry: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS)

EDUCATION
Ph.D. Chemistry, Northbridge University, 2023. Thesis: Vibrational probes of ion transport in nanoconfined membranes
M.Sc. Chemistry, Central Institute of Science, 2017
B.Sc. Chemistry, Riverside College, 2015

RESEARCH EXPERIENCE
Postdoctoral Fellow, Lakeshore University (2023-present)
- Resolved exciton migration in perylene diimide crystals with transient absorption microscopy
- Built Redfield and HEOM models of vibronic coupling in molecular aggregates
Graduate Researcher, Northbridge University (2017-2023)
- Used 2DIR spectroscopy to follow ion transport in nanoconfined membranes
- Measured ionic conductivity with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy

SELECTED PUBLICATIONS
1. Whitfield, D. K.; Ortega, M. Exciton migration in perylene diimide crystal polymorphs. J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2025, 16, 101.
2. Whitfield, D. K.; Chen, L.; Ortega, M. Vibronic coherence in molecular aggregates by 2DES. J. Chem. Phys. 2024, 160, 204.
3. Whitfield, D. K.; Park, S. Correlated ion hopping in nanoconfined polymer membranes. Nat. Commun. 2023, 14, 5521.
4. Whitfield, D. K.; Park, S. Ion transport and spectral diffusion in nanoconfined membranes. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2022, 144, 990.

AWARDS
Graduate Fellowship, Northbridge University, 2019
Best Poster Award, American Chemical Society National Meeting, 2021

TEACHING
Teaching Assistant, Physical Chemistry Laboratory, 2018-2020
